## Overview

This integration brings your **OpenMediaVault** NAS into Gladys, through its web interface on your local network:

- a **NAS** device: CPU and memory usage, uptime, packages to upgrade, version;
- a device per **disk**: temperature, standby, S.M.A.R.T. health;
- a device per **file system**: space used and free space;
- a device per enabled **service** (SMB/CIFS, NFS, SSH…): running or not;
- **scenes**: NAS unreachable or back, NAS restarted, updates available, reboot required, failing disk, file system almost full or missing, service stopped; and actions to read the status, run an rsync job, check for updates, reboot or shut down the NAS;
- three **dashboard widgets**.

![The widgets of the integration: overview, storage, one file system with its history, and disks (generated illustration, not a screenshot)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/William-De71/gladys-openmediavault/main/docs/assets/widgets.en.png)

Everything stays on your network: the integration only talks to OpenMediaVault, never to a cloud.

## Prerequisites

- Gladys Assistant 5.1.0 or later.
- OpenMediaVault 7 or 8 (tested on 8.5), reachable from the Gladys machine. OpenMediaVault 6 works without the standby of the disks.
- An **administrator** account of OpenMediaVault, without two-factor authentication: the `admin` account, or better a user dedicated to Gladys, member of the **openmediavault-admin** group (**Users > Users**, create the user, then tick the group). OpenMediaVault has no read-only role: every reading of the NAS needs the admin role.

| What the integration reads | Where OpenMediaVault shows it                 |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| CPU, memory, updates       | Dashboard, System > Update Management         |
| Disks, standby             | Storage > Disks                               |
| S.M.A.R.T. health          | Storage > S.M.A.R.T. > Devices                |
| File systems, threshold    | Storage > File Systems (column Usage warning) |
| Services                   | Diagnostics > Services                        |
| rsync jobs                 | Services > Rsync > Jobs                       |

## Configuration

In Gladys, open **Integrations > OpenMediaVault**, install it, then fill in:

| Field                          | What to enter                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Address of OpenMediaVault      | The address you type in your browser, for example `http://192.168.1.10` (add the port if it is not 80 or 443). |
| User                           | The administrator account, `admin` by default.                                                                 |
| Password                       | Its password. It is never shown again nor written in the logs.                                                 |
| Check the HTTPS certificate    | Only for an `https://` address: leave it off with a self-signed certificate.                                   |
| Reading interval               | 15 to 240 seconds, 60 by default (CPU, memory, file systems, services). The disks are read every 5 minutes.    |
| S.M.A.R.T. health of the disks | When no disk is in standby (default), every hour even if it wakes a disk, or never. See below.                 |
| Language of the texts          | Language of the names, states and scene summaries; automatic follows your dashboard.                           |

Click **Test the connection**: Gladys shows the name and the version of your NAS.

OpenMediaVault e-mails its administrator at the first login from a new browser: you get one such e-mail when the integration starts. The integration keeps the cookie that tells OpenMediaVault it already knows it, so no new e-mail comes at each restart.

## Usage

### Devices

Open **Integrations > OpenMediaVault > Discovery**: the NAS, its disks, its file systems and its enabled services are listed. Add the ones you want, in the room of your choice.

| Device      | Features                                                                   |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NAS         | CPU usage (%), memory usage (%), uptime (days), updates available, version |
| Disk        | Temperature (°C), power state (active, standby), S.M.A.R.T. health         |
| File system | Space used (%), free space (GB)                                            |
| Service     | Running (active or inactive)                                               |

A disk is recognized by its serial number: it keeps its device in Gladys even when Linux renames it (`/dev/sda` becoming `/dev/sdb`). A card reader or a virtual disk without a serial number is not offered. Every feature is a state: the commands are scene actions.

### Disks in standby

Reading the S.M.A.R.T. health of a disk spins it up when it sleeps. By default, the integration reads it every hour, but only when no disk is in standby: a NAS whose disks sleep at night is never woken up by Gladys. The temperature and the power state are read every 5 minutes without ever waking a disk (a sleeping disk has no temperature). With OpenMediaVault 6, which does not report the standby, choose **every hour** or **never**.

### Dashboard widgets

- **OpenMediaVault**: CPU and memory gauges, uptime, updates, disks, services, and the buttons **Check for updates**, **Reboot** and **Shut down** (both with a confirmation).
- **NAS storage**: how full each file system is, the fullest first, a missing one on top. Choose one file system in the settings to see its gauge, its free space and, once its device is added, the history of its usage.
- **NAS disks**: temperature, standby and S.M.A.R.T. health of each disk, failing disks first.

### Scenes

Triggers, in **Scenes > New scene > Trigger > OpenMediaVault**:

| Trigger                     | When                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NAS unreachable or back     | The NAS stopped answering (two readings in a row), or answers again. Not after a reboot asked from Gladys.    |
| NAS restarted               | Its uptime went back to zero: reboot, power cut.                                                              |
| Updates available           | Packages to upgrade appeared, or their number grew.                                                           |
| Reboot required             | An update needs a reboot.                                                                                     |
| Disk health changed         | The S.M.A.R.T. health of a disk became bad, reports a past problem, or is good again.                         |
| File system almost full     | A file system goes above, or back below, its usage warning threshold set in OpenMediaVault (85 % by default). |
| File system missing or back | A file system is no longer mounted (USB disk unplugged), or is mounted again.                                 |
| Service started or stopped  | An enabled service started or stopped.                                                                        |

Actions: **read the status** (CPU, memory, fullest file system, hottest disk, failing disks, stopped services, updates, and a summary for a message), **run an rsync job** (by its comment or UUID; waits up to 100 s and tells whether it completed), **check for updates** (installs nothing), **reboot** and **shut down** (with an optional delay).

Examples:

- When **a disk becomes failing** → send me `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}` on Telegram.
- Every night at 2 am → **run the rsync job** "Photos backup", then, if `status` is not `completed`, notify me.
- When **the file system "data" goes above its threshold** → notify me with `{{triggerEvent.data.free_gb}}` GB left.
- When the house is empty for a week → **shut down the NAS** (Gladys cannot switch it on again: plan Wake-on-LAN, a smart plug or the power settings of the NAS).

### Transport

Local only: the integration talks to the web interface of OpenMediaVault on your network, like your browser does, and nothing leaves your network. The catalog shows the **local** badge.

## Troubleshooting

- **"OpenMediaVault refused the user name or the password"**: check them by logging in to the web interface. The integration waits 10 minutes before trying again; **Test the connection** tries at once.
- **"This account is not an administrator"**: add the user to the **openmediavault-admin** group, or use `admin`.
- **"This account asks for a second factor"**: use an account without two-factor authentication.
- **"does not answer"**: check the address and its port, from the Gladys machine. If you open OpenMediaVault in `https://`, type `https://`.
- **The S.M.A.R.T. health stays "Not read"**: a disk is often in standby; choose **every hour** in the configuration, or check **Storage > S.M.A.R.T.** in OpenMediaVault.
- **A disk is missing**: OpenMediaVault does not report its serial number (some USB enclosures). It cannot be told apart reliably, so it is not offered.
- **The usage trigger never fires**: set the **Usage warning threshold** of the file system in **Storage > File Systems** (0 turns it off).
- Logs: **Settings > Supervision**, or the container logs. For more details, add the environment variable `DEBUG=gladys-integration-sdk` to the container.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings OpenMediaVault asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenMediaVault account | `section` | No | The integration logs in to the web interface of OpenMediaVault, like your browser, and reads it every minute. It needs an administrator: admin, or a user of the openmediavault-admin group, without two-factor authentication. Everything stays on your network. |
| Address of OpenMediaVault | `string` | Yes | The address you type in your browser to open OpenMediaVault, with its port if it is not 80 or 443. |
| User | `string` | Yes | An administrator of OpenMediaVault. |
| Password | `secret` | Yes |  |
| Check the HTTPS certificate | `boolean` | No | Only for an https:\/\/ address. Leave it off with the self-signed certificate of OpenMediaVault. |
| Options | `section` | No | OpenMediaVault e-mails its administrator at the first login from a new browser: you will get one such e-mail when the integration starts. |
| Reading interval (seconds) | `number` | No | CPU, memory, file systems and services. The disks are read every 5 minutes. |
| S.M.A.R.T. health of the disks | `select` | No | Read every hour. Reading it spins up a disk in standby: by default it waits until no disk sleeps. |
| Language of the texts | `select` | No | Names of the features and summaries of the scenes. Automatic: the language of your dashboard. |

## How to install OpenMediaVault in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: OpenMediaVault appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-openmediavault:0.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-openmediavault](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-openmediavault).

OpenMediaVault requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

OpenMediaVault is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [William-De71](https://github.com/William-De71), not by the Gladys core team.
